[[File:Euphorbia characias, Sète 01.jpg|thumb]]
'''''Euphorbia characias''''', the '''Mediterranean spurge'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref name=USDA>{{PLANTS | symbol =EUCH13 | taxon =Euphorbia characias | accessdate = 26 April 2015}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Euphorbiaceae]] typical of the [[Mediterranean vegetation]].
It is an upright, compact [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|1.2|m|0|abbr=on}} tall and wide.

==Description==
It has many medium to tall unbranched stems with long narrow leaves, clothed densely in short hair (tomentose), and dark (ssp characias) or yellow (ssp wulfenii) floral [[nectar gland]]s within the yellow cup-like [[cyathium|cyathia]], which are borne in large dense spherical to oblong clusters, from spring to early summer.<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> The fruits are smooth densely-hairy capsules. It is a tough plant, capable of resisting long periods of [[drought]]. It grows preferably in dry areas, often far away from the [[water table]], both in flat as well as in mountainous terrain. This plant can also resist high [[salinity]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.emasconsultors.com/pymegestio/platges/general/herbari/Herbari |title=Espècies d'habitats allunyades del freàtic |access-date=2010-10-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110710185032/http://www.emasconsultors.com/pymegestio/platges/general/herbari/Herbari |archive-date=2011-07-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="FoT"/>

Similar species include ''E. kotschyana'' (leaf uppersides shiny) and ''E. thompsonii'' (leaves hairy but upper leaves unexpectedly very short).<ref name="FoT">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 7 |author=Davis}}</ref>

==Subspecies==
Two main [[subspecies]] are found in different regions of the Mediterranean Basin; these often overlap in the western areas of distribution:.
* ''E. characias'' <small>L.</small> subsp. ''characias''. From Portugal to Crete (floral glands dark, stems to 80 cm<ref name="FEU">{{cite book |title=Flora Europaea, vol. 2 |author=Tutin}}</ref>).
* ''E. characias'' subsp. ''wulfenii'' <small>(Hoppe ex W.D.J.Koch) Radcl.-Sm.</small>. From Southern France to Anatolia (floral glands yellow, stems to 180 cm<ref name="FEU"/>).

==Cultivation==
''Euphorbia characias'' is valued as an ornamental plant for its ability to survive drought and its groundcovering capabilities. It is suitable for any location, sheltered or exposed, in light soil in full sun. It is fully hardy down to {{convert|-10 |C|F|abbr=on}}.<ref name=RHSAZ/>

===Cultivars===
Garden [[cultivar]]s are sold under the names ‘Black Pearl’, ‘Thelma's Giant’, ‘Lambrook Gold’, ‘Silver Swan’ and ‘Tasmanian Tiger’, among others. They come in a variety of colors, from silvery grey and bluish green to greenish yellow. These garden varieties are valued in Mediterranean or desert landscaping for not being highly demanding and for looking good despite lack of watering in sunny areas.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.naturaliajardiners.com/plantes/pag/fitxes/e/Euphorbia%20characias.htm |title=Mediterranean Landscaping |access-date=2010-10-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714160008/http://www.naturaliajardiners.com/plantes/pag/fitxes/e/Euphorbia%20characias.htm |archive-date=2011-07-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Uses==
This plant also has uses in [[Complementary and alternative medicine|traditional medicine]]; like many other species of genus ''[[Euphorbia]]''<ref>[http://www.botanical-online.com/alcaloideseuphorbiacatala.htm Lletereses] {{in lang|ca}}</ref> its [[toxic]] white and sticky [[sap]] has been used to treat skin excrescences, like cancers, tumors, and warts, since ancient times.
